question: How many critical highway segments are outlined in the report on India’s Priority Corridors for Zero-Emission Trucking for the adoption of zero-emission trucks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The report on **India’s Priority Corridors for Zero-Emission Trucking** identifies **Ten critical highway segments** for the adoption of zero-emission trucks (ZETs).
 
• These corridors were selected based on factors like **freight volume, economic importance, and environmental impact**.
 
• The adoption of zero-emission trucks along these corridors is aimed at **reducing greenhouse gas emissions** and promoting sustainable transport systems in India.
 
• The identified corridors are part of a larger strategy to transition India’s **transport and logistics sector** towards cleaner energy alternatives.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s commitment to achieve **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070**, as outlined at the **UN Climate Change Conference (COP26)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Zero-Emission Trucks (ZETs):**

 
 
• ZETs are vehicles powered by **electricity or hydrogen fuel cells**, producing no tailpipe emissions.
 
• They play a crucial role in reducing air pollution and mitigating the **impact of climate change**.
 
• Examples include **electric trucks** like Tesla Semi and hydrogen-powered trucks from companies like Toyota and Nikola.
 
• In India, the adoption of ZETs is gaining momentum due to government incentives and advancements in battery technology.
 
 
 
• **India’s Freight Corridors:**
 
 
• India’s freight corridors are the backbone of its logistics and transport sector, connecting major cities and industrial hubs.
 
• Examples include the **Golden Quadrilateral**, which links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata, and the **Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs)** under construction.
 
• The identified ten critical highway segments are likely to include parts of these high-traffic routes, ensuring maximum impact of ZET adoption.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Trucking:**
 
 
• The transport sector contributes around **13.5% of India’s total greenhouse gas emissions**, with trucking being a major contributor.
 
• Transitioning to zero-emission trucks can significantly reduce **carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions** and improve air quality, particularly in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched several programs, such as the **Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles (FAME)** scheme, to promote the use of electric vehicles (EVs), including trucks.
 
• Policies like the **National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP)** aim to make India a global hub for electric vehicle manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Several countries, including the US, China, and members of the European Union, are adopting **zero-emission trucking technologies** to meet their climate goals.
 
• India’s emphasis on zero-emission trucks aligns with global efforts to decarbonize the transport sector and achieve **climate resilience**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Challenges:**

 
 
• High initial costs of ZETs compared to diesel trucks.
 
• Limited **charging infrastructure** and range anxiety among fleet operators.
 
• Need for policy support and subsidies to make ZETs economically viable.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• With advances in battery technology and declining costs, the adoption of ZETs is expected to rise significantly in the coming years.
 
• Collaborations between the **public and private sectors** can accelerate the development of charging infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Success:**
 
 
• Countries like Norway and the Netherlands have made significant progress in deploying zero-emission trucks through policy incentives and infrastructure development.
 
• India can learn from these global examples to overcome challenges and achieve its sustainability goals in the transport sector.
